@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+# Roc text counter world
+
+The no-Screen legacy-text world program used by `id`'s multiplayer service.
+Unlike `../roc-counter`, it imports no platform modules at all: `view` and
+`layout` return the plain UTF-8 text `count=N`, which the host presents as-is
+rather than as a screen document. The host owns the authoritative state; guests
+send `inc`, and every participant sees the returned `count=N` presentation over
+either Iroh or WebSocket. It also demonstrates the `records` export
+(structured data mirroring).
+
+This example is deliberately minimal: it exists so the legacy text
+presentation path — a world that never imports `Screen` — stays covered
+end-to-end over the browser websocket (issue #3181), including compilation
+under a capability ceiling that excludes `Screen`.
+
+## Build
+
+Requires Zig 0.16 and the Roc nightly that generated
+`../roc-world/host/src/roc_platform_abi.zig` (currently
+nightly-2026-10-04-130536d). From this directory:
+
+```sh
+ROC=/path/to/roc ZIG=zig ./build.sh
+```
+
+The world platform lives once in `../roc-world` and is shared by every example
+app (see `../roc-world/README.md`). The checked-in `roc_platform_abi.zig` there
+is generated Roc ABI code; keep the compiler build pinned when regenerating.
+`build.sh` builds the freestanding Zig host, compiles `main.roc` against it,
+then validates the result with `wasm-tools`.
+
+## Run a hosted world
+
+```sh
+id serve --world --world-admin-token "$WORLD_ADMIN" --world-module text-counter.wasm
+```
+
+Each server offers one named world (`--world-name`, default `lobby`), stored
+under `.id-worlds/<name>/`; run several servers to offer several worlds.
+
+Or leave out `--world-module` and install a compiled module while the world is
+running:
+
+```sh
+id world install HOST_NODE text-counter.wasm --admin-token "$WORLD_ADMIN" --addr HOST_IP:PORT
+```
+
+`id world invite HOST_NODE --admin-token "$WORLD_ADMIN" --name Ada` prints a
+guest capability. Join with `id world join HOST_NODE --capability TOKEN`; type
+`/input 696e63` to increment and ordinary lines to chat. The browser view at
+`http://localhost:PORT/world` uses the same session protocol.
+
+The program also publishes structured records (`records : Model -> Str`):
+
+```sh
+id world records HOST_NODE --capability TOKEN      # {"count": N}
+id world mirror HOST_NODE --capability TOKEN --follow        # live replica
+id world mirror HOST_NODE --capability TOKEN --dir ./replica # durable replica
+```
+
+`records` reads the host's current set; `mirror` replicates it peer-to-peer
+over iroh-docs, so a replica keeps receiving changes. Records are bounded
+(<= 4096 keys, keys <= 256 bytes without control characters, values <= 8 KiB,
+1 MiB total) and are recomputed from the program, never stored as a second
+source of truth.
+
+The module has no Wasm imports. The host applies fuel, memory, module-size and
+message-size limits. A trap fails closed: that world program is marked
+unhealthy and must be reinstalled. A non-ephemeral world keeps its installed
+module and journal under `.id-worlds/lobby/`, so state survives restarts by
+deterministic replay.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
+export ROC="${ROC:-roc}"
+source ../roc-toolchain.sh
+WASM_TOOLS="${WASM_TOOLS:-nix run nixpkgs#wasm-tools --}"
+
+if [ -z "${WASM_OPT:-}" ]; then
+  if command -v wasm-opt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    WASM_OPT="wasm-opt"
+  else
+    STORE_OPT=$(ls -d /nix/store/*-binaryen-*/bin/wasm-opt 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
+    if [ -n "$STORE_OPT" ] && [ -x "$STORE_OPT" ]; then
+      WASM_OPT="$STORE_OPT"
+    else
+      WASM_OPT="nix shell nixpkgs#binaryen --command wasm-opt"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
+# The world platform (host adapter + ABI) is shared by every app.
+(cd ../roc-world && ./build-host.sh >/dev/null)
+
+# Built without --debug and shrunk below (F11.15, #555) so the checked-in
+# module stays <= 1 MiB; the strip step keeps the name section, so
+# Wasmtime trap traces still resolve function names.
+"$ROC" build main.roc --target=wasm32 --wasm-memory=8454144 --output=text-counter.wasm
+
+# Shrink the checked-in module (F11.15, #555): optimize with wasm-opt
+# and strip DWARF/custom sections so modules stay <= 1 MiB. --all-features:
+# Roc nightly emits post-MVP features that binaryen rejects by default. The name
+# section is kept so Wasmtime trap traces still resolve.
+$WASM_OPT -Os --all-features text-counter.wasm -o text-counter.wasm.opt
+mv text-counter.wasm.opt text-counter.wasm
+$WASM_TOOLS strip text-counter.wasm -o text-counter.wasm.stripped
+mv text-counter.wasm.stripped text-counter.wasm
+
+# Reject accidental imports before the module is advertised to a world host.
+$WASM_TOOLS validate text-counter.wasm
+echo "Built text-counter.wasm (import-free Roc legacy-text world module)"

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+app [program] { pf: platform "../roc-world/platform.roc" }
+
+## The no-Screen legacy-text world: this program imports no platform
+## modules at all. `view` returns plain UTF-8 text (`count=N`), which the
+## host presents as-is instead of a screen document.
+
+Model := { count : I64 }
+
+program = { init, update, view, layout, records, wants, snapshot, restore }
+
+init : U64 -> Model
+init = |_seed| { count: 0 }
+
+## Events are matched exactly: only "inc" increments.
+update : Model, U64, Str -> Model
+update = |model, _pid, ev| if ev == "inc" { count: model.count + 1 } else model
+
+## The counter renders as plain text, not a screen document.
+view : Model -> Str
+view = |model| "count=${model.count.to_str()}"
+
+## Legacy text does not reflow: every viewport gets the same plain text.
+layout : Model, U64, U64 -> Str
+layout = |model, _width, _height| "count=${model.count.to_str()}"
+
+## Structured data the host stores and replicates: a JSON object of records.
+records : Model -> Str
+records = |model| "{\"count\":${model.count.to_str()}}"
+
+## This program wants nothing from the server.
+wants : Model -> Str
+wants = |_model| "{}"
+
+## The model as text. `restore(snapshot(m))` must behave exactly like `m`; the
+## host checks this before it trims the world's journal.
+snapshot : Model -> Str
+snapshot = |model| model.count.to_str()
+
+restore : Str -> Model
+restore = |text| match I64.from_str(text) {
+    Ok(count) => { count: count }
+    Err(_) => { count: 0 }
+}
